subject: eastern-han
place: China; precise findspot not specified here
caption: Pottery architecture made for a burial context. Its range spans the first through early third century; it is not dated precisely to 200 CE.
alt: Green glazed pottery watchtower with tiered roofs, balconies and a walled base.
additionalImageAlts: Frontal colour view of the green watchtower, showing the stacked balconies and rooflines.
Black-and-white side view of the same model. The narrow profile shows how far the roof and balconies project.
notice: Which parts look like a building?
Which features can you describe before guessing their purpose?
relevance: Architectural model, elite estate context and afterlife provision.

subject: colima
caption: A roofed building on a platform, possibly once an incense-burner lid. Current catalogue: 200 BCE–200 CE.
alt: Small ceramic model of a peaked-roof building on an elevated rectangular platform.
additionalImageAlts: Frontal view of the peaked roof and the short stairway ascending the platform between two raised corner features.
notice: What supports the roof?
What makes the proposed function more than a visual observation?
relevance: Compare architectural form and tentative use with the Han tower without asserting contact.
datingNote: Current catalogue: 200 BCE–200 CE. Pillsbury’s 2015 essay captions the same accession 200 BCE–300 CE. Current catalogue followed; discrepancy preserved.

subject: eastern-han
caption: A Han granary model brings storage and provisioning into a burial setting.
alt: Black-and-white photograph of a cylindrical pottery granary on short feet, with a broad round roof and a small rectangular opening near the base.
notice: What parts might relate to storing food?
relevance: Investigate estate work alongside the watchtower.

subject: eastern-han
caption: A well-head model broadens the architectural story from protection to water.
alt: Black-and-white photograph of a round well-head model with an arched frame rising from the rim and a small fitting at the top.
notice: How might water be lifted?
relevance: Compare water provisioning and funerary models.

subject: roman-world
place: Roman world; precise manufacture and findspot not specified here
caption: Julia Domna’s portrait engraved into beryl, approximately 200–210 CE. A small image participates in dynastic representation.
alt: Blue-green, roughly rectangular gem with bevelled edges. The engraved profile of Julia Domna shows rows of waves in her hair.
notice: Which features identify this as a portrait?
How does a small object carry a large political message?
relevance: Imperial authority, Syrian connections and the political work of images.

subject: roman-world
caption: A funerary portrait of Eutyches, 100–150 CE. Parts of its Greek inscription have competing translations.
alt: Painted portrait of a young person with short dark hair, white tunic and large dark eyes.
notice: Where does light seem to strike the face?
What can the inscription add to the image?
relevance: Identity, freed status and mixed practices in Roman Egypt.

subject: roman-world
place: Roman world; this specimen is not identified as excavated at Aksum
caption: A third-century Roman grape-shaped bottle. The Aksum essay compares this type with an excavated example; it does not give this specimen an Aksum findspot.
alt: Small molded glass vessel shaped like a cluster of grapes with a narrow neck.
notice: What shape has the glassmaker borrowed from nature?
relevance: Separate type comparison from the provenance of an individual object.

subject: palmyra
caption: A Palmyrene family’s funerary relief with named figures and ancestors in an Aramaic inscription.
alt: Limestone relief with a reclining man and three smaller figures beside an inscription.
notice: How are the figures arranged?
What does naming people add to our understanding?
relevance: Family commemoration in a city connected to caravan exchange.

subject: kushan-contexts
caption: A gold coin of Kanishka, catalogued approximately 130 CE. Coin imagery supports a question about royal representation, not every person’s beliefs.
alt: Gold coin showing a standing ruler with a surrounding inscription.
additionalImageAlts: Reverse of the gold coin. A standing figure extends an arm beside an animal, with lettering around the rim.
notice: What can you distinguish on each side?
What would you need to establish where it circulated?
relevance: Royal imagery, monetary standards, dating uncertainty and find-context limits.

subject: teotihuacan
caption: A heavy greenstone face dated to the third–seventh centuries. The museum suggests attachment to another object rather than wearing by a living person.
alt: Broad carved stone face with narrow eye recesses, a projecting nose and a partly open mouth.
notice: Are there holes that would allow a wearer to see?
relevance: Material observation can constrain functional interpretation; the object belongs to a later range than an exact 200 CE snapshot.

subject: moche
caption: A modeled serpent wraps around a stirrup-spout bottle. The meaning of its imagery remains uncertain.
alt: Rounded Moche ceramic bottle with a raised snake curling around its body and an arched spout.
notice: Where does the animal’s body go?
Which features seem unlike an ordinary snake?
relevance: Distinguish material technique, imagery and uncertain interpretation.

subject: moche
caption: A seated figure becomes part of a vessel, dated 200–500 CE.
alt: Moche ceramic stirrup-spout bottle modeled as a seated human figure.
notice: How are figure and container combined?
relevance: Modeled human representation and specialized ceramic work.

subject: dongson
caption: A bronze drum in miniature, with four frogs. The broad catalogue range does not establish one exact year or one agreed function.
alt: Small bronze drum with a flared base, decorated surface and four frog figures on top.
notice: Can you find all four frogs?
How might the uses of a miniature and a full-size drum differ?
relevance: Non-state material traditions, circulation, miniature scale and uncertain function.

subject: benin-ivory
place: Court of Benin(?), Nigeria; qualified museum attribution
caption: Portuguese men interpreted by a Benin ivory carver, c. 1525–1600. Poses and dress distinguish rank.
alt: Carved ivory saltcellar supported by Portuguese figures in detailed hats and clothing.
notice: Which figures face outward?
How does the carver distinguish rank?
relevance: African artistic agency, commissioning and representation of foreign patrons.

subject: kongo-translation
caption: A cast-brass crucifix dated to the sixteenth–seventeenth centuries. Local artistic choices complicate a simple story of copying.
alt: Brass crucifix with a central Christ figure and additional small figures around the arms.
notice: How are the additional figures placed?
What can form alone tell us about a user’s beliefs?
relevance: Translation of Christian forms, local meaning and uncertainty in provenance.

subject: mughal-books
caption: A folio made around 1590–95 depicting Krishna protecting villagers. The making date is not the date of the sacred story.
representedDate: A sacred narrative; no historical event year assigned.
alt: Colorful manuscript painting of Krishna lifting a mountain above gathered villagers and animals.
notice: How does the artist arrange the protected people?
How is the sheltering mountain made visible?
relevance: Courtly translation and manuscript invention; sacred representation distinguished from eyewitness evidence.

subject: ming-workshops
caption: A mid-sixteenth-century porcelain jar decorated with fish and lotus plants. This specimen is not identified as galleon cargo.
alt: Large round porcelain jar with orange carp and water plants painted around its surface.
notice: How many fish can you follow around the surface?
Which materials and colors required specialized work?
relevance: Imperial production, technique and comparison of intended audiences.

subject: manila-network
caption: Mexican tin-glazed earthenware, c. 1680–1700. A later chapter in the Pacific exchange story, after the journey’s 1450–1650 focus.
alt: Blue and white decorated ceramic jar with a broad body and narrow base.
notice: What differs between this earthenware jar and the Chinese porcelain jar?
relevance: Later American transformation within the wider network; chronology made explicit.

subject: uruk-accounts
caption: A probable grain account, c. 3100–2900 BCE. Missing verbs limit precise interpretation.
alt: Small rectangular clay tablet incised with pictographic signs and round numerical impressions.
additionalImageAlts: Other face of the clay tablet, with groups of wedge-shaped and circular impressions separated by lines.
notice: Which marks repeat?
Which claims need interpretation beyond what you can see?
relevance: Economic recordkeeping, work and the limits of early textual interpretation.

subject: old-kingdom
place: Saqqara, cemetery north of Djoser complex, tomb QS915, documented excavations
caption: An elite chapel wall showing offerings, music and senet, c. 2465–2389 BCE. The present arrangement includes a displaced element.
alt: Painted limestone tomb wall with tall false-door panels and smaller rows of people, offerings and musicians.
notice: How do the sizes of figures differ?
Can you find activities beyond the large portraits?
relevance: Daily-life representation in a selective funerary setting; recarving and museum arrangement.

subject: dholavira
place: Indus Valley; not identified here as a Dholavira find
caption: An ancient seal with a modern impression, c. 2600–1900 BCE. The carving’s signs have not been fully deciphered.
representedDate: Ancient seal; accompanying impression is modern.
alt: Square Indus seal with a one-horned animal and signs, alongside a modern positive impression.
additionalImageAlts: Black-and-white photograph of the back of the seal, showing a raised grip on the square slab.
notice: How does the impression reverse the carved design?
Can an unread sign still tell us something about making and use?
relevance: Distinguish the ancient object, modern impression, uncertain reading and regional attribution.

subject: liangzhu
caption: A jade cong, c. 2400 BCE, with a square exterior and round bore. Function and meaning remain uncertain.
alt: Tall dark jade cong with a square tapered exterior, circular opening and faint carved faces at the corners.
notice: What changes when you look from the top?
Can you locate the small faces?
relevance: Skilled work, social status, uncertain ritual meaning and separate city/culture/object chronologies.

subject: kerma-potters
place: Excavated in Abydos, Egypt, tomb 525; Kerma ceramic tradition

dateOverride.label: c. 1802–1640 BCE
dateOverride.note: Visible catalogue range retained. API objectEndDate repeats -1802 and is corrected from the record’s Date field.

caption: A Kerma beaker found in an Egyptian grave. Its location is known; the owner’s origin is a tentative interpretation.
alt: Thin-walled bell-shaped pottery beaker with a polished red body, black rim and iridescent transition band.
notice: How do the two surface colors meet?
Which claim requires more than looking at the pot?
relevance: Skilled firing, documented findspot and the limits of inferring a person’s identity.

subject: shang-ritual
place: China; broad Shang attribution, no precise findspot supplied here

dateOverride.label: Shang period, c. 1600–1046 BCE; no narrower object date supplied
dateOverride.note: The record has no displayed narrow Date. Its Period supplies only this broad attribution.

caption: An inscribed oracle bone attributed to the Shang period. No translation of this particular specimen is supplied without support.
alt: Long pale fragment of animal bone with small incised Chinese signs across its surface.
notice: How are the signs placed on the available surface?
What would you need before claiming a translation?
relevance: Selectivity of ritual writing and honest dating precision.

subject: olmec
caption: A ceramic female figure, 1200–900 BCE. Adornment and modeled features invite questions about social identification.
alt: Small modeled ceramic female figure with wide eyes, styled hair and ear ornaments.
notice: Which features are modeled carefully, and which are exaggerated?
What can adornment suggest without identifying an individual?
relevance: Small-scale representations, social identities and attributed ritual interpretations.

subject: nimrud-palace
caption: A protective figure from Ashurnasirpal II’s palace, c.883–859 BCE. Its museum setting differs from its original room.
alt: Carved gypsum relief showing a winged bearded figure in patterned dress.
notice: What suggests protection or authority?
How does stone change the scale of a message?
relevance: Royal representation, skilled labor and reconstructed display.

subject: athens-water
caption: A water jar with women at a fountain, c.510–500 BCE. A represented scene is not a census of later Athenian life.
alt: Black-figure terracotta water jar showing women with vessels at a fountain house.
notice: Find the lifting and pouring handles.
What work does the scene show?
relevance: Daily work, public water and the limits of using images as social evidence.

subject: taharqo
place: Probably from Taharqo’s pyramid at Nuri, Sudan

dateOverride.label: c.690–664 BCE
dateOverride.note: Displayed catalogue reign range; API end repeats -690 and is corrected from the Date field.

caption: A royal shabti of Taharqo; the Nuri origin is probable.
alt: Black-and-white photograph of a standing stone funerary figure with a headdress, crossed arms and lines of writing on the lower body.
notice: Which details identify a royal figure?
What does “probably” change in an object label?
relevance: Funerary labor, Kushite kingship and qualified provenance.

subject: chavin-textile
place: Peru; said to come from the southern coast
caption: Painted cotton, fourth–third centuries BCE, with imagery related to Chavín. The reported origin does not reveal a complete route.
alt: Fragmentary pale cotton textile painted with a large fanged figure and curling serpent-like forms.
notice: Which shapes recur?
How might a cloth travel differently from a carved wall?
relevance: Revised chronology, portable imagery and uncertain provenance.

subject: byzantium
caption: Mid-tenth-century ivory icon; the missing wings once formed a triptych. Probable private devotional use is an interpretation.
alt: Small carved ivory icon with a central cross, standing figures and an architectural canopy.
notice: Where might the lost side panels have fitted?
How would the size affect use?
relevance: Separate object chronology, devotional setting and political frame.

subject: abbasid-craft
caption: Tenth-century luster-painted bowl with figures and a blessing inscription.
alt: Cream-colored shallow bowl painted in metallic brown with a seated figure and two birds.
additionalImageAlts: A second overhead photograph of the bowl in brighter light, showing the seated figure and curving decoration against the pale glaze.
notice: How does light change the painted surface?
Where is the inscription?
relevance: Technique, imagery and the diversity of settings within Islamic art.

subject: tang-city
caption: An earthenware court lady, seventh–eighth century. The figure is not identified as a named person.
alt: Standing painted earthenware woman in a long robe with hands held in front of her.
notice: What details of dress survive?
Which personal details remain unknown?
relevance: Elite burial representation and limits of biography.

subject: maya-vessel
caption: A seventh–eighth-century Maya vessel. Its ownership text does not identify the ruler’s polity.
alt: Tall ceramic vessel with incised seated ruler, hieroglyphic text and supernatural imagery.
notice: Where do text and image overlap?
What claims need a decipherment rather than visual observation?
relevance: Food, ownership, rank and uncertain regional attribution.

subject: middle-niger
place: Inland Niger Delta, Mali; no secure excavated context asserted
caption: A thirteenth-century terracotta figure. Its original purpose and the meaning of its markings remain uncertain.
alt: Terracotta seated person curled around one raised knee with the head resting sideways.
additionalImageAlts: Rear view of the curled seated figure, showing rows of raised bumps down its rounded back.
notice: Describe the posture without naming a feeling.
Turn to the back view: what marks can you see?
relevance: Skilled modeling, uncertain meaning and urbanism beyond a single state model.

subject: song-art
caption: An eleventh–twelfth-century stoneware tea bowl with streaked “hare’s-fur” glaze.
alt: Dark round tea bowl with brown streaks radiating across its glazed interior.
notice: How does the glaze change toward the rim?
What would a photograph of the bottom add?
relevance: Craft at the scale of a hand-held object within broader artistic and political histories.

subject: inca-weaving
place: Peru; highland technique with coastal comparisons
caption: A camelid-hair tunic dated1450–1550. Its historical range remains intact across chapter boundaries.
alt: Wide Andean tunic with black and white upper stripes and jagged stepped lower bands.
notice: Where do different patterns meet?
Can you identify two joined pieces?
relevance: Skilled work, regional comparison and chronology crossing a political rupture.
